wy_e_five_ten_wall.blurb: A single-pitch sport wall on the Main Wall at Wild Iris, in the high country near Lander. It holds 17 bolted lines, and the grades cluster hard in the 5.10 range, with six more at 5.11 and only a handful of easier warm-ups from 5.7 to 5.9. That makes it a steady choice for a day of mid-grade mileage rather than a place with much variety. It sits between two steeper, harder walls, so stronger partners can wander over for something tougher. The trail along the cliff band reaches it directly, and the short walk from the main path is signed.

wy_gneiss_canyon.blurb: A steep little side canyon off the Laramie River Canyon in the Laramie Range, running roughly east to west with big boulders strewn along its floor. The gneiss is strong and offers crack systems with some face climbing between them. Nearly everything here is bolted, 16 sport lines against a single trad route, and the grades start around 5.8 and reach 5.12, with the bulk of the climbs in the 5.10 and 5.11 range. It is a compact spot, reached by a hiking trail rather than a roadside pull-in, so expect a bit of a walk and not much company.

_expect.name: Gully Wall, AKA Dr. Seuss Wall, The

wy_gully_wall_aka_dr_seuss_wall_the.blurb: The first sizable wall met when walking the old road down into lower Shoshone Canyon, just west of Cody. A big gully splits the cliff, and the rock rises in blobby, odd shapes above the paved road. There are 17 routes in the granite of the Lower Canyon: nine sport, seven trad and one top-rope line. Grades run from 5.6 up to 5.13, though most sit between 5.10 and 5.12, so it suits climbers past the beginner stage. One four-pitch 5.10 sport line is the highlight for many visitors.
wy_gully_wall_aka_dr_seuss_wall_the.parking_note: Leave the car at the pullout farthest west on the south side of the highway as it runs through Shoshone Canyon, then walk down to the old road below.

wy_mid_mountain.blurb: A bouldering sector on the shady north side of Cedar Mountain, west of Cody, among cedar trees and good sandstone blocks. There are 17 problems, spread from V0 to V8, with most of them landing around V2 and V3 and a few much harder lines at the top end. It is the closest bouldering to the road in its drainage, with a short walk over a hill and down into the trees. Because the aspect is shady, it feels pleasant in the warmer seasons but cold in winter. The stone is softer than some sandstone areas, so avoid it after moisture.

wy_riverside_wall.blurb: A wall on the north side of lower Shoshone Canyon, down by the river west of Cody. The area is known for featured, fractured rock with good friction, and spring and fall are the best seasons here. Riverside Wall is a harder-end venue: 13 sport routes and four trad lines, running from 5.9 to 5.13 with nearly all of them between 5.11 and 5.12. Climbs on this side of the canyon above the road catch good sun, which helps on cooler days. It is not a place for those still working up through the moderates.

wy_the_shooting_gallery.blurb: A sport wall in Rogers Canyon, north of Laramie, on the north side of the road past the Dark Side and the Amphitheater, spotted easily by its bolted lines. It was among the first walls climbed in the canyon, first as a top-rope spot, and fresh bolting began there in 2019. All 17 routes are sport, and the grades go from 5.8 to the low 5.13s, with the largest group at 5.12. Most lines have lowering hardware at the top, so turning around is simple. Expect short, sustained climbing on a crag better suited to experienced sport climbers.

_expect.name: Ice Box (later renamed by some ... Jurassic Park)

wy_ice_box_later_renamed_by_some_jurassi.blurb: A quiet cliff at Vedauwoo, outside Laramie, known for excellent rock and a good supply of moderate cracks, with a few bolted lines mixed in. Of its 16 routes, twelve are trad and four are sport, ranging from 5.5 to 5.11, with the harder 5.11s making up the biggest single group. The climbs are short, mostly 40 to 80 feet, so it works for quick laps. Reaching it takes a hike along the base of the main cliffs, up and over a pass and a steep drop to the base, which keeps the crowds thin compared with the roadside formations.
